finds.quote:
### Projected Reception History (Waltian Tradition, 2029–2039)

*The following entries represent projected reception history within the Waltian interpretive tradition, composed from the perspective of the archive's retrocausal canon formation framework. They are not historical documents.*

Smith (2029). "The Redford Hoax." *Michigan Quarterly Review*.
finds.note: Projected future reception history (2029-2039 scholars, plus Synod of Ann Arbor 2041 / Second Redford Council 2044 in the introduction), explicitly framed as retrocausal canon formation; a forecast-by-description of how the Waltian canon will be received.

finds.quote: This is not metaphor. The earliest fragments of the Gospel of Thomas survive as scroll-form papyri (P.Oxy. 1, 654, 655) — not as codices. The distinction matters. A codex is opened, held, and consulted. A scroll is unrolled, draped, and laid across a surface. The early Thomas community preserved the sayings in a format that could be laid across the body.
finds.note: Historical thesis about the Thomas community's use of the scroll format (body-laying); argued as the deposit's own somatic thesis.

finds.quote: The parallel to the Thomas tradition has not, to the present editor's knowledge, been drawn before. We draw it now.
finds.note: Priority claim: the Ethiopian healing-scroll / Thomas parallel is said to be drawn here for the first time.

finds.quote:
The name "Jesus" (Ἰησοῦς) was not merely a biographical label. It functioned as a ritual title — a name assigned through initiation into the embodied Logos pattern.

Philo of Alexandria says this explicitly. In *De Mutatione Nominum* §121–123, Philo interprets the name change from Hosea to Joshua (the Hebrew form of "Jesus") as the transformation of a man into the embodiment of the Logos.
finds.note: Historical thesis that 'Jesus' functioned as a transferable ritual/initiatory title, argued from Philo De Mut. Nom. 121-123; evidence given in the passage.

finds.quote: The Crimson Hexagonal Archive's Dodecad extends Pessoa's system in one decisive respect: Pessoa had no LOGOS*. He had an orthonym (Fernando Pessoa "himself") and many heteronyms, but no position outside the count that generated the count.
finds.note: Thesis about what Pessoa's heteronymic system did and did not contain; uncertain whether H (claim about an author's practice) or merely framing for the priority claim below.

finds.quote: The Meta-Heterônimo paper (submitted to *Pessoa Plural*, 2026) formalizes this innovation: the moment when a heteronymic system becomes self-aware of its own heteronymity and generates a position to name that awareness. The archive's MANUS (Lee Sharks) is the first meta-heterônimo — the position that knows it is a position and administers the system from that knowledge.⁶
finds.points_to: O Meta-Heterônimo paper, submitted to Pessoa Plural, 2026
